chapter: Mellophone, Brunswick records and the West End Roof
title: First recording with Johnny Hyman and the Red Nichols style
summary: His first record was with Johnny Hyman, with named players, patterned on Red Nichols's 'futuristic' music.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: What was your first record that you ever made, I wonder?
First record I ever made was with Johnny Hyman.
Drums on that record. Did you do anything else?
There's some singing on some of those. Huh? There's some singing on some of those Johnny Hyman songs. Oh, I don't know.

I don't know. I don't know. Maybe some of the ones that we made up at WSMB. But this was for Victor. Yeah. Uh, Alligator Crawl. And that band was Dias, Horace Dias on piano. Nappy LeMond on the guitar. Elroy Mays on clarinet. Charlie Hartman on trombone. Johnny and myself. And, and, and, huh? A bass? No bass. No.
And the kid playing, Alvin, Alvin Gertro playing harmonica. Guy playing harmonica like a cornet.
Did you work with that band or was it just?
No, that band was just made up for, for, for that recording. Oh, I, Johnny worked in, in Schilling's band. That was just about the time that we were both playing with, with Schilling.
Was there a particular style you were aiming for in that record, the band?

Johnny was aiming for, for Red Nichols. Uh huh. That's before he, that's before he started imitating Bix. Uh huh. He imitated Nichols. He used to try to play exactly like Nichols. So that's, the arrangements were built around Nichols. That's about, about the time when, when Red was making all those, uh, records with the,
Five pennies and all, yeah. With the pennies.
